data.narrative:
Blue Origin operates in Space & Aerospace at the SPAC stage, having raised over $10B to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space, though no single peer matches Blue Origin's scale and funding profile across stage and tier simultaneously.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum threshold requirements; while 14 total Space & Aerospace peers exist, narrowing to stage and valuation tier yields fewer than 3 datapoints. Public-comp anchoring cannot be deployed because Blue Origin's revenue is not disclosed, precluding meaningful P/S multiple application. The Space & Aerospace public median trades at 27.4x revenue across the 5-ticker set, but this metric alone provides no actionable anchor without the target's top-line figure.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods reflects a structural valuation challenge common to ultra-late-stage, privately-held aerospace companies: Blue Origin's scale and capital intensity place it outside conventional peer clustering. Any valuation estimate would require either disclosure of revenue and profitability metrics, or reliance on precedent transaction analysis and management guidance—neither present in the available data. The $10B+ cumulative raise establishes a floor for loss capital but does not imply enterprise value.
